chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Abdul Hamid al-Ta'i, from Al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'A servant does not find the taste of faith until he leaves lying, whether in jest or in earnest.'
ai.seo_question: What condition must be met for a person to truly experience the 'taste of faith' according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes that the experiential reality of faith (dhawq al-iman) is inextricably linked to the comprehensive abandonment of lying, extending beyond formal oaths to include casual jest (hazl). Shia scholars emphasize this universality to refute the notion that 'light' lies are permissible, asserting that truthfulness is a foundational attribute of the believer's character. This teaching underscores the holistic nature of Iman, where internal conviction manifests consistently in all modes of communication.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Urwa, from Abdul Hameed Al Ta’iy, from Al Asbagh Bin Nubata who said,
‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘A servant cannot find the taste of the Emān until he leaves the lies, its vain ones and its serious ones’.
en.sarwar: 11. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah from ‘Abd al-Hamid al-Ta’I from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah who has said the following: “
Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) has said, ‘A servant (of Allah) does not sense the taste of belief until he stays away from lies, serious ones as well as trivial ones.’”
